why: The tree claims that choices tracked expected value, but nothing in it records that the strength of that sensitivity was the same across the three conditions.
The tree's only risk-attitude claim is the null difference in risk premiums; the fitted risk-aversion parameter rho, and its Study 1 difference between Social and Solo, appears in no claim.
No claim covers the fitted risk-aversion parameter rho — the tree records only the null risk-premium comparison, which points the other way.
The tree claims the Responsibility model beat the alternatives but records nowhere that it failed to beat the Guilt-envy model in Study 1.
The claim states that a responsibility-weighted model of happiness fits better than models without responsibility weighting, which is this comparison against the Basic model.
A pointer to the Methods and a figure supplement describing how the parameters were checked, not a finding stated here.
Both halves are in the tree: happiness tracks lottery outcomes (happiness-correlates-partner-reward) and being the decision-maker changes it (agency-reduces-happiness).
This is the guilt interaction itself — happiness falling further after a partner's loss when the participant was the one who chose — which the claim states without the numbers.
The tree claims the guilt effect after negative partner outcomes but never records the companion null after positive ones, which is what makes the effect specific to harm.
The tree claims precuneus, TPJ and mPFC respond more in Social than Solo; it does not claim this narrower result, that only precuneus and TPJ peak when the lottery is chosen in the Social condition.
A pointer to the appendix table rather than a result stated here.
No claim covers the outcome phase contrast of lottery against safe outcomes; the tree's striatal claims are about the moment of choosing, not of receiving.

The tree claims precuneus, TPJ and mPFC in Social versus Solo; that only precuneus and TPJ survive both comparisons, and only for risky choices, is a sharper result no claim carries.
